web-host.lisp:275-280
(fnn-os-error () nil)
(sb-bsd-sockets:socket-error () nil)
(error (condition)
  (if (and (find-class 'fnn-tls-error nil) (typep condition 'fnn-tls-error))
      nil
    (error condition)))
The thread body (314-326) handles only sb-bsd-sockets:socket-error. fnn-web-request (247-262) calls fnn-web-open, then later fnn-web-close, with no unwind-protect between them.
fix: Wrap the :open..:close span in an unwind-protect that runs fnn-web-close for any cid that was opened. In the accept-loop thread, route non-socket conditions to fnn-owner-fault-service as fnn-control-accept-loop does, or log the condition and continue for a connection-scoped refusal.
notes: 10-02 22:32 coded on lane/host-lifecycle 4e409a9d6 (handed to runner); see lanedumps/host-lifecycle.md for verification
reviewer: fnn-web-serve (web-host.lisp:275-280) re-raises every error that is not an os, socket or TLS error. The thread lambda (web-host.lisp:314-326) handles only sb-bsd-sockets:socket-error. The images are saved with --disable-debugger (build.lisp:622), so an unhandled error in this thread exits the whole process with code 1, not the owner's 3 or 4. That is worse than the reported 'web face dies silently'. Errors that reach this path include: fnn-fault outside any owner-serialized call (fnn-web-slice at web-host.lisp:63, 'more events than ACL2 allows' at 225, malformed-action faults), which never fenced the owner; and fnn-web-open's 'owner service is stopping' refusal (owner.lisp fnn-owner-serialized), which during an exit-3 stop can replace the uncertain code with 1. The leaked-session part is moot because the process dies, although fnn-web-request does lack an unwind-protect between :open and :close.
scenario: Several things raise an fnn-store-error inside fnn-web-request: an ACL2 slice fault (fnn-web-slice at 253), the event-cap fault (225), or fnn-web-open's 'owner service is stopping' refusal during a stop. None of these stop the owner, despite the comment "an ACL2 fault is the owner's (it stopped)". The error is re-raised out of fnn-web-serve and out of the thread lambda unhandled. Under --disable-debugger, an unhandled error in a thread ends the process abruptly with SBCL's code, not the owner's 3 or 4. At best the web face dies silently while the node keeps serving NNTP. If the error came after :open, the logical reader connection and its exposure slot (fn-owner-exposure-open) are never closed or released, so per-address exposure limits fill up until restart.
title: Web face thread lets non-socket errors escape the thread, and an opened owner session is never released on that path
